subject: Integration next steps & Dedicated sizing — technical deep-dive scope
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Keller <mkeller@finserv.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Integration next steps & Dedicated sizing — technical deep-dive scope

Hi Morgan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the technical deep-dive with your engineering and procurement teams.

Summary of what we heard (please flag anything we missed):
- Primary use: transaction enrichment and policy/risk scoring in real-time (low single-digit-second tail latency).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~150–250 inference requests/sec, with bursts to ~400rps during market open.
- Typical prompt size: 250–500 input tokens; expected returned tokens average ~120.
- Key features: structured output + tool calling for enrichment, embeddings for historical similarity and reranker for top-K.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + customer-managed keys (KMS) are required; data retention window ~30 days.

Integration checklist items (what we need to validate in the deep-dive):
1) SDK & auth model: your preference for service-account-like API keys vs. mTLS + short-lived tokens. We support both; we recommend short-lived tokens with KMS integration for Private/Dedicated.
2) Routing & failover: plan for primary region + automatic fallback to a secondary region if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
3) Structured output/tool calls: need to confirm how many external tool calls per request (1–3 expected) and whether you require synchronous tool invocations.
4) Embeddings / reranker: expected index size (approx docs), and peak similarity lookup QPS.
5) Dedicated sizing inputs: target SLO (p50/p95 latency), average tokens per request, desired concurrency per model replica.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf (basic questions we will run through in the deep-dive).

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm the expected peak rps and your p95 latency SLO for the user-facing path?
- Please share a small sample of typical prompts (sanitized) and an estimate of documents in the embedding index.
- Proposed time for the technical deep-dive with eng + security: Tues/Wed next week (Nov 24/25) — we can do a 60–90 minute session.

I’ll have Marissa and Ben bring a preliminary Dedicated sizing proposal and an autoscale policy template to the call.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao

Thanks, Aditya — this summary looks right. A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive:

- Auth: we prefer short-lived tokens that our platform can rotate via KMS. mTLS would be acceptable for on-prem components later. Can you confirm Redwood supports automatic token rotation and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated?
- Tool calling: most calls will be synchronous (policy enrichment calls to our internal rule engine). Expect 1–2 external tool calls per request.
- Embeddings: rough index size is ~12M vectors initially; expected similarity lookups of 800–1,200 qps during peak. We plan to batch updates overnight.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 1.0s for standard inference path (end-to-end); p95 <= 1.5s when external tool calls are included.

Procurement: please share any standard SLA or templates we should review.

We can do the deep-dive Wed Nov 25 at 10:00am EST — that works for engineering and security.

Morgan Keller
Head of Platform Engineering — FinServ Solutions
mkeller@finserv.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Morgan — looping in a bit of technical detail in advance of Wed so the deep-dive is productive. I put together an initial Dedicated sizing proposal attached. Highlights below.

Preliminary Dedicated sizing assumptions (ballpark):
- Target steady-state: 200 rps served by Dedicated fleet optimized for 350-token average length and 120-token outputs.
- Peak handling plan: 400rps handled via burst capacity + autoscale buffer (2x baseline) — recommend reserved capacity for baseline, burst configured with short-lived GPU pods.
- Concurrency per model worker: 8 concurrent requests per replica using batching optimizations. This assumes quantized model (bf16->int8 path) and sequence-length aware kernels.
- Queueing & throttling: employ per-customer request queue with soft concurrency limit and priority lanes for real-time vs batch/async. If queue depth > 2500, fallback to a lower-cost model variant or route to hosted fallback.
- Autoscale policy: scale on token throughput (tokens/sec) + p95 latency signals; maintain at least 20% headroom for traffic spikes.

Embeddings & reranker guidance:
- For 12M vectors we recommend a sharded ANN (approx 6–8 shards) with dedicated CPU/FPGA-backed nodes for heavy similarity queries, fronted by small GPU rerankers to apply contextual scoring.
- Batch similarity QPS windowing: accept 800–1,200 qps via 10–20ms per-shard average, then rerank top-200 candidates on GPU.

Auth & KMS:
- Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS with short-lived tokens (we issue ephemeral inference credentials that can be minted via your identity provider). HSM integrations available upon request (we use standard KMS APIs + HSM-backed key storage in our Private offering).

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-proposal.xlsx (sizing workbook), sla_appendix.docx (SLA + compliance notes).

Planned agenda for Wed deep-dive (60–90m):
1) Quick recap (5m)
2) Auth/KMS and network (15m)
3) Serving runtime & concurrency (20m)
4) Embeddings pipeline and reranker architecture (15m)
5) Autoscale, queues, and failover policies (15m)
6) Action items & mutual action plan (10m)

If you can share an anonymized sample prompt set and confirm whether tool calls are strictly synchronous, we can run a short throughput sim pre-call.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Morgan — quick note from the throughput/embeddings side:
- We can run a synthetic load test ahead of Wed if you can provide a sanitized prompt set and a sample of IDs for the 12M vector index shape. That will validate shard sizing and reranker batch sizes.
- For reranker: start with top-200 candidate rerank, GPU batch size 256 for scoring; this generally keeps p95 rerank time <60ms if the model is optimized.
- Concurrency knobs: recommend starting with 8 conc/replica and iterating after a smoke run. If you need stricter p95 SLAs we can drop to 4 conc/replica for latency-sensitive routes.

I’ll book the Wed 10:00am EST slot and create a brief runbook for the load test steps.

Ben Carter
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
